title: Introduce FlashWave attention kernel with rotary coalescing and KV preheat
author: Asha Kapoor
release_notes: Adds FlashWave: a new attention kernel combining a FlashAttention-derived fastpath with rotary coalescing and KV preheat support. Opt-in via runtime flag `ATTN_KERNEL=flashwave`. Improves tail latency and throughput for mixed-length workloads.
description: Context: PROD incidents over the past quarter exposed p99 tail spikes for mid-length (256-1024) sequences when concurrent continuous-batching and KV warmup overlapped with cold starts. Motivation: provide a unified kernel that (1) keeps the hotpath of FlashAttention-style fused matmul+softmax fast, (2) coalesces rotary/rope math into contiguous operations to reduce memory traffic, and (3) exposes a light-weight KV preheat/reservation so warmup hits happen before latency-sensitive requests. This PR introduces FlashWave, an opt-in kernel and scheduler hints to orchestrate warmup without changing public API. What changed: added runtime/attn/flashwave_kernel.* implementing fused qkv->flashwave path, a rotary_coalesce helper that reorganizes rotary multiplications for cache-friendly access, a scheduler hint path (scheduler/jitter_preheat.cpp) that issues low-priority preheat requests during low tail utilization windows, and a KV reservation layer (runtime/kv/preheat.h) to reserve KV slots for pinned sessions. Also added unit+integration tests and perf harness updates. Compatibility: backward compatible; kernel selected by config or auto-probe fallback to legacy flashbridge if unsupported hardware or model shape. Rollout: feature-gated behind ATTEN_KERNEL=flashwave and runtime flag runtime.opt.flashwave.enable; staged canary on Dedicated for 48h then widen. Performance summary: typical p50 unchanged, p95 reduced by ~12-20% for seq 512-1024 depending on batch shape; throughput up to +8% for cross-model mixes. See benchmark_results for numbers.
